It elected a new member of the [[United States House of Representatives]] to replace [[Kevin McCarthy]], who resigned on December 31, 2023, following his [[Removal of Kevin McCarthy as Speaker of the House|removal]] as [[Speaker of the United States House of Representatives|speaker of the House]].{{cite news|last=Karni|first=Annie|author-link=Annie Karni|date=December 6, 2023|title=McCarthy says he will leave Congress at the end of the year|work=[[The New York Times]]|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2023/12/06/us/politics/kevin-mccarthy-congress.html|access-date=December 6, 2023}} Two Republicans, [[Tulare County]] Sheriff Mike Boudreaux and state assemblyman [[Vince Fong]], advanced to the runoff. Boudreaux narrowly edged out the leading Democrat, teacher Marisa Wood, to claim the second runoff spot. Fong won the runoff with more than 60% of the vote{{Cite web |date=2024-05-21 |title=California lawmaker Vince Fong wins special election to finish ousted House Speaker McCarthy's term |url=https://apnews.com/article/house-california-kevin-mccarthy-republicans-vince-fong-f6d82faba1a853c354d597c5bcd5c85f |access-date=2024-05-22 |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |last=Blood|first=Michael }} and won a full term in [[2024 United States House of Representatives elections in California#District 20|November 2024]]; Boudreaux dropped out of the November race but his name remained on the ballot.{{Cite web |date=2024-07-01 |title=Sheriff Mike Boudreaux suspends congressional campaign for Kevin McCarthy's former office |url=https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2024-07-01/mike-boudreaux-suspends-campaign-for-congress-endorses-vince-fong-bakersfield-tulare-kevin-mccarthy |access-date=2024-07-05 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}} == Background == {{further|January 2023 Speaker of the United States House of Representatives election|Removal of Kevin McCarthy as Speaker of the House}} At the start of the [[118th United States Congress|118th Congress]], Republicans' narrow majority garnered from the [[2022 United States House of Representatives elections|2022 elections]] allowed McCarthy, the then-leader of the [[House Republican Conference]], to be [[January 2023 Speaker of the United States House of Representatives election|elected speaker]] at the start of the session. However, opposition from the far-right [[Freedom Caucus]] prolonged the election, leading to fifteen rounds of voting that eventually resulted in McCarthy's election. The caucus continued its opposition of McCarthy during his tenure, threatening a [[Government shutdowns in the United States|government shutdown]] following his involvement in negotiations for the [[2024 United States federal budget|federal budget]]. When McCarthy led the House in passing a [[continuing resolution]], relying on votes from the [[House Democratic Caucus|Democratic Caucus]] to effectively avert a shutdown, Representative [[Matt Gaetz]] of [[Florida]] filed a [[Motion to vacate the chair|motion to vacate]] the speakership. On October 3, the motion narrowly passed, and McCarthy was [[Removal of Kevin McCarthy as Speaker of the House|removed from the office of Speaker of the House]], the first instance of which in American history. Two months after his political defeat, McCarthy published an [[op-ed]] with ''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'' announcing his resignation from Congress, highlighting his accomplishments and stating that his work is "only getting started."{{cite news |title=I'm Leaving the House but Not the Fight |first=Kevin |last=McCarthy |author-link=Kevin McCarthy |work=[[The Wall Street Journal]] |date=December 6, 2023 |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/kevin-mccarthy-my-next-chapter-house-gop-retirement-california-e4e593d7 |url-access=subscription |access-date=December 6, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231206162634/https://www.wsj.com/articles/kevin-mccarthy-my-next-chapter-house-gop-retirement-california-e4e593d7 |archive-date=December 6, 2023}} His announcement came while House Republicans' majority had already lowered since the [[Expulsion from the United States Congress|expulsion]] of Representative [[George Santos]] of [[New York (state)|New York]], making the legislative agenda of the new speaker, [[Mike Johnson]] of [[Louisiana]], more difficult to pass. As such, Republicans see both the special and general [[2024 United States House of Representatives elections|House elections in 2024]] as crucial to maintaining their influence in Congress.{{cite news |title=Kevin McCarthy to leave Congress at the end of this year |first=Melanie |last=Zanona |work=[[CNN]] |date=December 6, 2023 |access-date=December 6, 2023 |url=https://www.cnn.com/2023/12/06/politics/kevin-mccarthy-resigning/index.html}} Nonetheless, this district is considered [[Safe seat|safely Republican]]: McCarthy won 67.2% of the vote in [[2022 United States House of Representatives elections in California#District 20|2022]] against Democratic challenger Marisa Wood. == Nonpartisan blanket primary == === Campaign === [[Vince Fong]], an assemblymember who was considered a protégé of McCarthy, announced that he would be running for the seat after initially declining to run. He was deemed ineligible to run in the 2024 Presidential Primary as the deadline already passed (but not ineligible for the special election) by [[California Secretary of State]] [[Shirley Weber]] due to Fong having already qualified to be on that ballot for [[2024 California State Assembly election|re-election]] in the [[California State Assembly]], which is prohibited by state law.{{cite web|url=https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2023-12-15/setting-up-legal-fight-california-election-officials-say-vince-fong-cant-run-for-congress|title= California elections officials say Assemblymember Vince Fong can't run for Congress in Bakersfield |date=December 15, 2023|author=Nelson, Laura J.|website=[[Los Angeles Times]]}}{{cite web|url=https://thehill.com/homenews/house/4363558-mccarthy-mentee-vince-fong-ineligible-for-congress/|title= McCarthy mentee Vince Fong determined ineligible for congressional candidacy |author=Robertsno, Nick|date=December 16, 2023|website=[[The Hill (newspaper)|The Hill]]}} Fong sued the state, with Superior Court judge Shelleyanne W. L. Chang ruling in favor of Fong and allowing him to run in the election.{{cite web|url=https://www.politico.com/news/2023/12/28/mccarthy-protege-can-run-for-congress-after-court-win-00133297|title= McCarthy protege can run for Congress after court win |website=[[Politico]]|author=Mason, Melanie|date=December 28, 2023}} In response to the ruling, Weber appealed the ruling and assemblymember [[Wendy Carrillo]] introduced a bill that would prevent candidates from running for two elected offices at the same time.{{cite web|url=https://www.sacbee.com/news/politics-government/capitol-alert/article283881818.html|title=Southern California Democrat introduces bill in 'direct response' to Vince Fong congressional run|author=Hatch, Jenavieve|website=[[The Sacramento Bee]]}}{{cite web|url=https://sjvsun.com/news/politics/weber-files-notice-of-appeal-to-remove-fong-from-ballot/|title=Weber files notice of appeal prohibit Fong from running, while assemblywoman [[Gail Pellerin]] introduced a bill to bar candidates from filing to run for more than one office during the same election.{{cite
